summary: RTSP (RFC 2326, superseded by RFC 7826) is present in recce ONLY as a servicefp signature in svcdetect.py:102 (matches `^RTSP/\d`). There is no port-name entry in svcdetect PORT_NAMES for 554/8554, no serviceenum.py _NAME/_PORT wiring, no recce/services/rtsp.py module, no vulndb entries for the four dominant camera vendors (Hikvision/Dahua/Axis/Foscam), and no defaultcreds table for IP cameras. RTSP is one of the highest-density attack surfaces in modern enterprise networks (physical security, meeting rooms, warehouse cams, hospital wards) and is almost entirely uninspected today. A proper module would mirror the SIP module's shape — OPTIONS/DESCRIBE fingerprint, Digest auth-realm capture, default-cred pass, well-known path enumeration — with a feed into a NEW `known_streams` cross-service surface plus contributions to `known_users`, `known_hostnames`, and `known_hashes` (hashcat mode 11400 covers RTSP Digest as it does SIP).

files: recce/services/svcdetect.py:102 — signature-only (`^RTSP/\d` → `rtsp`); NOT in PORT_NAMES so a nudged/banner-less 554 stays labelled unknown
recce/services/serviceenum.py — no `rtsp` in _NAME, no 554/8554 in _PORT, so `recce services` emits no next-step command for open RTSP ports
recce/services/ — no rtsp.py module (contrast: sip.py, ipp.py, vnc.py all exist)
recce/creds/defaultcreds.py — no camera-vendor default credential table
recce/vuln/vulndb.py — no Hikvision / Dahua / Axis / Foscam / ONVIF entries
existing_coverage.notes: Effectively zero coverage. Only signal recce produces today is 'this port speaks RTSP' when a banner nudge happens to elicit an RTSP status line.

capabilities.name: port-registry-wire
capabilities.description: Add 554 and 8554 to svcdetect.PORT_NAMES ({554: ('rtsp','Real-Time Streaming Protocol'), 8554: ('rtsp-alt','RTSP (alt)')}), add 'rtsp': 'rtsp' to serviceenum._NAME and 554/8554 → 'rtsp' to _PORT, and register 'rtsp' in scripts/recce-service.sh. Without this an open 554 keeps its 'unknown' label whenever nmap fails to elicit the banner, and `recce services` emits no next-step command.
capabilities.protocol_reference: RFC 2326 §18.1 (IANA-assigned ports 554/tcp+udp); RFC 7826 §22.1 (RTSP 2.0 keeps 554); IANA rtsp-alt on 8554/tcp

capabilities.name: options-fingerprint
capabilities.description: Send `OPTIONS rtsp://<ip>:<port>/ RTSP/1.0` with CSeq: 1 and User-Agent. Parse the response's `Server:` header (camera model+firmware — e.g. `Server: Hipcam RealServer/V1.0`, `GStreamer RTSP server`, `H264DVR 1.0`, `Dahua Rtsp Server`) and `Public:` header (allowed verbs — GET_PARAMETER means heartbeat works, ANNOUNCE/RECORD means writable RTSP push). One packet, no auth, always answered. Primary fingerprint.

capabilities.name: describe-sdp-harvest
capabilities.description: Send `DESCRIBE rtsp://<ip>:<port><path> RTSP/1.0` with `Accept: application/sdp`. On 200 OK parse the SDP body: `s=` (session name — often hostname/model), `i=` (info), `a=tool:` (encoder brand), `a=control:` (per-track control URIs), `m=video`/`m=audio` (codec + payload types — H.264/H.265/MJPEG), `a=rtpmap` (clock rate), `a=fmtp` (SPS/PPS reveals resolution/profile). SDP is the highest-value artifact this service produces. Requires unauth stream or valid creds.

capabilities.name: auth-realm-disclosure
capabilities.description: Capture the 401 challenge. `WWW-Authenticate: Digest realm="...", nonce="...", algorithm=MD5, qop="auth"` — realm is almost always vendor-branded (`IP Camera`, `HikvisionDS`, `Login to <MAC>`, `AXIS_<serial>`, `IPCam`). Also flag when BOTH Basic AND Digest are offered (cleartext downgrade) or Basic-only (creds go plaintext on the wire the moment a client authenticates).

capabilities.name: unauth-stream-detection
capabilities.description: If DESCRIBE (or SETUP) returns 200 without an Authorization header ever being sent, the stream is world-viewable. Critical for any camera reachable from an untrusted segment — a scanner can confirm this in one round trip. Also test the Hikvision quirk `?authbasic=YWRtaW46MTEK` and Dahua magic-query bypass paths.
capabilities.protocol_reference: RFC 2326 §10.2, §10.4 (SETUP); OWASP IoT Top 10 I2 (Insecure Network Services)

capabilities.name: well-known-path-enum
capabilities.description: Vendors ship documented, unchanging URIs. Probe DESCRIBE against a small curated table: Hikvision `/Streaming/Channels/101`, `/h264/ch1/main/av_stream`, `/ISAPI/Streaming/channels/101`; Dahua `/cam/realmonitor?channel=1&subtype=0`, `/live`; Axis `/axis-media/media.amp`, `/mpeg4/media.amp`; Foscam `/videoMain`, `/videoSub`; ONVIF-generic `/onvif/media`, `/live/main`; GStreamer `/test`, `/stream`. Response codes (200 vs 401 vs 404) disambiguate vendor even when Server header is stripped and tell you which stream a valid cred would unlock.
capabilities.protocol_reference: Hikvision ISAPI IP Media Device Protocol §7; Dahua HTTP API v2.76 §5.1; Axis VAPIX v3 (media/stream); Foscam CGI SDK

capabilities.name: default-cred-check
capabilities.description: Bounded (≤12 pairs, 1 pair/sec) Digest attempt against the discovered realm using industry-known camera defaults: admin/12345 (Hikvision pre-2015), admin/admin (Dahua/Foscam), root/pass and root/root (Axis pre-2018), admin/<blank>, admin/888888 (Dahua backdoor era), service/service (Bosch), ubnt/ubnt (Ubiquiti UniFi Video). Honour recce's global auth-attempt budget; back off on 429. Feed discovered creds into recce's Credential store so downstream modules (SMB, SNMP) can try them.

capabilities.name: digest-challenge-capture
capabilities.description: Persist the Digest realm+nonce+algorithm+qop from the 401 into loot as a hashcat-ready line (`$sip$*<realm>*<uri>*<method>*<nonce>*<nc>*<cnonce>*<qop>*<response>` — hashcat mode 11400 covers RTSP the same way it covers SIP because the KD/H construction is identical). Recce cannot recover the client response unless a client authenticates in the scan window, but stashing the server challenge lets an operator run a subsequent capture or MitM their own client and feed hashcat directly.
capabilities.protocol_reference: RFC 7616 §3.4 (response computation); hashcat mode 11400 (SIP Digest MD5) — identical HA1/HA2 to RTSP Digest

capabilities.name: tls-rtsps-probe
capabilities.description: 8554 also carries RTSP-over-TLS in some GStreamer/Live555 deployments and enterprise VMS (Milestone, Genetec). Try a TLS handshake first on 8554 (svcprobe already has the primitive) — if it succeeds, tunnel OPTIONS through TLS and feed the presented cert into recce's known_hostnames via probes.py cert_covers (CN on IP-camera certs is usually MAC/serial/model — high-signal identifier).
capabilities.protocol_reference: RFC 2326 §19.2 discusses SSL layering; IANA rtsps assignment (322/tcp historic, 8554 in modern deployments)

capabilities.name: rtsp-http-tunnel-probe
capabilities.description: RTSP-over-HTTP tunneling (Apple/QuickTime spec, still implemented by Live555, Wowza, some VMSes): client sends `GET /path HTTP/1.0` with `x-sessioncookie: <id>` on 80/8080 and a paired POST on the same URL to bidirectionally tunnel RTSP. Detects RTSP hiding behind an HTTP front-end (common when a camera is behind a reverse proxy). Extend recce's HTTP probe to recognise the tunnel signature (`Server: DSS/`, `x-server-ip-address`, `application/x-rtsp-tunnelled`).
capabilities.protocol_reference: Apple QuickTime Streaming Server RTSP-over-HTTP tunneling spec (1999); Live555 RTSPOverHTTPServer

capabilities.name: get-parameter-liveness
capabilities.description: After OPTIONS reports GET_PARAMETER in Public:, send one `GET_PARAMETER *` with no body — the RTSP-standard keepalive. Confirms the service is genuinely live (not a stray SYN-ACK from a load balancer) and, for some servers, echoes `Session:` timeout hints and `Date:` (drift vs recce clock is a soft NTP-adjacency signal fed to ntp.py).

capabilities.name: camera-model-cve-map
capabilities.description: Add a curated table to vulndb.py mapping normalized (vendor, model, firmware) → CVEs. Minimum launch set: Hikvision CVE-2021-36260 (unauth RCE via ISAPI, KEV), CVE-2017-7921 (auth bypass); Dahua CVE-2021-33044/33045 (auth bypass), CVE-2013-6117 (backdoor); Axis CVE-2018-10660..10664 (multiple pre-auth), CVE-2022-31199; Foscam CVE-2018-6832. Keyed off the Server header + SDP `a=tool` extracted by options-fingerprint / describe-sdp-harvest.

capabilities.name: onvif-adjacency
capabilities.description: An RTSP-answering port almost always has an ONVIF SOAP endpoint on the same host at 80/8080/8899 (`/onvif/device_service`). When RTSP is confirmed, flag http.py to probe those paths for `GetDeviceInformation` (unauth on many builds) and `GetCapabilities` — ONVIF returns manufacturer, model, firmware, serial, hardware ID as one SOAP response. Also flag hashcat mode 25100 (ONVIF WS-UsernameToken PasswordDigest — SHA1(nonce+created+password)) if a challenge is captured.
capabilities.protocol_reference: ONVIF Core Specification v22.06 §5.11 (Device Management); OASIS WS-Security UsernameToken Profile 1.1 §3.1

capabilities.name: credentials-in-url-catch
capabilities.description: If any prior recce observation (nmap script output, HTTP referrers, config dumps, SDP a=control lines) contains `rtsp://user:pass@host/...`, extract and file the credential — RTSP URIs still routinely carry inline creds in operator docs and NVR configs, and the ffmpeg/vlc command-line convention normalizes this. One regex over already-collected text; zero new traffic.
capabilities.protocol_reference: RFC 2326 §3.2 (rtsp URL syntax inherits RFC 3986 userinfo)

cross_service_wire_candidates: known_users: contribute camera-default usernames (admin, root, guest, service, ubnt, operator, viewer, MediaAdmin) once recce/services/rtsp.py sees an RTSP port — feeds SMB/SNMP/WinRM/SSH sprays without any per-service duplication (mirror recce/services/ipmi.py:604-621 pattern that pulls known_users)

known_hostnames: feed the SDP `s=` session name, the RTSPS certificate CN/SAN (via probes.cert_covers at probes.py:288), and any ONVIF GetDeviceInformation Manufacturer+SerialNumber — camera hostnames are almost always MAC or serial-derived and become high-quality reverse-DNS / AD-search seeds

known_hashes: emit RTSP Digest challenges as hashcat mode-11400 lines (identical construction to SIP Digest) and ONVIF PasswordDigest as mode 25100; both feed the existing creds.known_hashes / hashloot pipeline

NEW `known_streams` (proposed 6th shared surface): {url, transport, codec, resolution, auth_required, vendor, model, firmware} — consumed by report generation (docx.py can render a camera-inventory table) and by future attack-path graphs (an unauth camera in the DMZ + a workstation in office = pivot). This is the RTSP equivalent of relay_targets — a service-produced list of actionable endpoints downstream code queries by shape, not by service name. Follow core/relay_targets.py file shape (write_known_streams(hosts, out_path)).

NEW `known_devices` (proposed 7th shared surface, generalization): {vendor, model, firmware, host, evidence_service} — populated by RTSP, ONVIF, IPMI, SNMP sysDescr, UPnP; consumed by vulndb for CVE mapping and by known_hostnames for identifier inference. RTSP is the natural first citizen because it discloses model with zero auth on nearly every camera in the field.

creds.Credential store (existing): any default-cred hit gets written back so downstream modules retry the pair — cameras and NVRs share creds with the servers around them far more often than expected (same IT team, same password policy)

relay_targets: not directly applicable — cameras aren't SMB relay peers — but a compromised NVR (Linux/ARM box with root) is a valid pivot; contribute to a broader `pivot_targets` list if that surface is later added

recommended_findings.title: RTSP DESCRIBE discloses SDP: <n> tracks, codec, resolution — enables targeted attack
RTSP server discloses vendor/model via OPTIONS Server header
RTSP offers Basic authentication — credentials sent in cleartext
RTSP Digest realm discloses camera identity (<realm>)
ONVIF endpoint co-located with RTSP — full device info unauth
RTSP-over-HTTP tunnel detected on <port> (RTSP hidden behind HTTP)
RTSP credentials found in URL/config: rtsp://<user>:<pass>@...
RTSP port 554/8554 open (no dedicated recce probe today)

recommended_hashcat_modes.description: SIP Digest MD5 — identical HA1/HA2 to RTSP Digest per RFC 7616; use for captured RTSP 401 challenges once a client response is intercepted
ONVIF WS-UsernameToken PasswordDigest (SHA1(nonce+created+password)) — for the co-located ONVIF endpoint on the same camera
NTLM — enterprise VMS front-ends (Milestone, Genetec) sometimes proxy RTSP behind NTLM-auth HTTP; fallback

implementation_notes: Mirror recce/services/sip.py exactly — it is the closest structural analogue (text-header protocol, OPTIONS fingerprint, Digest realm capture, bounded enumeration secondary pass, findings + runbook + analyze). Create recce/services/rtsp.py at ~500 LOC with: is_rtsp(port), _options()/_describe()/_get_parameter() wire builders, probe(ip, port, timeout, tls=False), rtsp_targets(hosts), findings(hosts, probes), findings_to_vulns delegating to svccommon (matches sip.py:312-314), runbook (openRTSP / ffprobe / cameradar), analyze(hosts, creds, active, budget, progress) using svcprobe.iter_probe. Additions elsewhere: (1) svcdetect.py PORT_NAMES gets 554 and 8554; (2) serviceenum.py _NAME gets 'rtsp':'rtsp', _PORT gets 554/8554 → 'rtsp'; (3) scripts/services/ gets an rtsp helper, recce-service.sh gets the mapping; (4) creds/defaultcreds.py grows a CAMERA_DEFAULTS table (vendor → [(user,pass),...]); (5) vuln/vulndb.py grows a small camera-CVE table keyed on normalized (vendor,model); (6) core/known_streams.py added as the new cross-service surface (follow core/relay_targets.py shape); (7) cli surfaces the module in `recce services` output. Airgap constraint respected — all probes are stdlib socket/ssl. RTSP Digest lines emitted in hashcat-11400 format so no new cracker integration is needed.
